stem: A charge nurse is planning RN assignments for a shift that includes clients with substantially different acuity and nursing-care needs. Which principle should guide the assignments?

options.A: Use equal client counts as the primary balancing method once every assignment is within RN scope of practice.
options.B: Match client acuity and care needs with each nurse's competence, total workload, and available unit resources rather than relying on client numbers alone.
options.C: Prioritize geographic grouping of rooms because reducing walking distance is the best indicator of a safe nursing workload.
options.D: Rotate the most complex clients among nurses without considering demonstrated competence so difficult assignments are distributed evenly over time.

rationale: The 2026 NCSBN test plan directs RNs to prioritize care based on client acuity and, under Assignment, Delegation and Supervision, to assign or delegate according to client needs and personnel competency. It also requires recognition and use of available resources. Therefore, a safe assignment cannot be determined by client count, room geography, or equal rotation of complex cases alone; the charge nurse must consider acuity, care demands, nurse competence, workload, and resources together.
educational_objective: Construct nursing assignments by integrating client acuity and care needs with nurse competence, workload, and available resources rather than using equal numbers alone.
source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
source_locator: Management of Care activity statements, printed p. 7: prioritize delivery of care based on acuity and recognize/utilize resources; Appendix A, printed p. 20, Assignment, Delegation and Supervision: identify tasks based on client needs, assign/delegate to personnel with competency, and evaluate staff ability.
source_claim_supported: NCSBN requires prioritization based on acuity and assignment/delegation according to client needs, personnel competency, and available resources.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Appendix A, printed p. 20, Management of Care → Assignment, Delegation and Supervision; Management of Care activity statements, printed p. 7.
blueprint_topic: Management of Care — assignment, acuity, competence, workload/resources

source_original.stem: A charge nurse assigns one RN a client needing frequent complex wound care, another with unstable hemodynamics, and two stable clients. Which principle should guide the assignment?

options.A: Use equal patient counts as the main rule even when acuity and required nursing care differ substantially.
options.B: Match client acuity and care needs with nurse competence, workload, and available resources rather than relying on numbers alone.
options.C: Give the most complex clients to the least experienced nurse so difficult assignments are distributed evenly.
options.D: Base assignments mainly on room location because geographic efficiency outweighs differences in acuity.

source_original.rationale: The current NCSBN test plan directs nurses to prioritize care based on acuity and to make assignments/delegations according to client needs and personnel competency while considering available resources. Equal numbers alone do not establish a safe workload.
source_original.source_detail: Management of Care — prioritization by acuity and ‘Assignment, Delegation and Supervision’ based on client needs/personnel competency; recognition of available resources. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care; Assignment, Delegation and Supervision; prioritization/continuity/client rights as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Rewrote the stem to test the assignment principle without implying that a particular unsafe assignment had already been made. Replaced exaggerated distractors with realistic but incomplete assignment heuristics and recalibrated difficulty from hard to medium because the item tests a single core management principle.

audit_findings.clinical_category: Charge-nurse assignment — acuity, competence and workload
audit_findings.exact_locator: Management of Care activity statements and Appendix A Assignment, Delegation and Supervision.
audit_findings.claim_audit: No staffing ratio or numeric workload rule is asserted.

distractor_audit.A: Equal counts alone omit acuity/care demands.
distractor_audit.C: Geography may affect efficiency but is not the primary safety determinant over acuity/competence.
distractor_audit.D: Equal rotation cannot supersede demonstrated competence and client needs.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only B is sufficiently complete to guide safe assignment.
audit_findings.cueing: Distractors are plausible management heuristics rather than absurd errors.
audit_findings.blueprint: Direct Assignment, Delegation and Supervision mapping.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Confirmed B does not create an unsupported nurse-to-patient ratio and that difficulty is better calibrated as medium.
